title: Pronombres de Objeto Directo — Practice
description: Authored A2/B1 practice set for direct object pronouns: identifying the direct object, agreeing lo/la/los/las, placement before the verb or attached to infinitives, gerunds and commands, and neuter lo.

lessons.summary: The direct object is what the verb acts on — the answer to '¿qué?' or '¿a quién?'. In 'Compro el libro', 'el libro' is the direct object, and the pronoun that replaces it is: me, te, lo, la, nos, los, las. Third person agrees in gender and number with the noun it replaced: el libro → lo, la película → la, los libros → los, las llaves → las. Placement has two rules. Before a conjugated verb the pronoun stands alone in front of it: 'Lo compro', 'No lo compro'. With an infinitive, a gerund or an affirmative command it attaches to the end: 'Voy a comprarlo', 'Estoy leyéndolo', '¡Cómpralo!'. With an infinitive or gerund both positions are correct — 'Lo voy a comprar' and 'Voy a comprarlo' mean exactly the same thing — but a negative command only allows the front position: 'No lo compres'. Note the accent that appears when attaching keeps the original stress: leyendo → leyéndolo, compra → cómpralo. There is also a neuter 'lo' that stands in for a whole idea rather than a noun: '¿Sabes qué hora es? — No, no lo sé.' In parts of Spain you will hear 'le' for a male person (leísmo); 'lo' is the form used across Latin America and the one to produce here.

examples.english: Are you buying the book? — Yes, I'm buying it.
Are you watching the film? — Yes, I'm watching it.

examples.spanish: Lo voy a comprar. / Voy a comprarlo.
examples.note: both positions are correct with an infinitive
attached in affirmative commands, in front in negative ones
neuter lo — it replaces an idea, not a noun

items.prompt: ¿Compras el libro? — Sí, ___ compro.
items.promptEnglish: Are you buying the book? — Yes, I'm buying it.
items.explanation: 'El libro' is masculine singular → lo.

items.prompt: ¿Ves la película? — Sí, ___ veo.
items.promptEnglish: Are you watching the film? — Yes, I'm watching it.
items.explanation: 'La película' is feminine singular → la.

items.prompt: ¿Tienes las llaves? — Sí, ___ tengo.
items.promptEnglish: Have you got the keys? — Yes, I've got them.
items.explanation: 'Las llaves' is feminine plural → las.

items.prompt: ¿Conoces a mis hermanos? — Sí, ___ conozco.
items.promptEnglish: Do you know my brothers? — Yes, I know them.
items.explanation: People can be direct objects too (marked by personal 'a'). Masculine plural → los. 'Les' is the indirect object form.

items.prompt: ¿Quieres el café? — Sí, ___ quiero.
items.promptEnglish: Do you want the coffee? — Yes, I want it.
items.explanation: Agreement follows the noun's gender, not the speaker's: el café → lo.

items.prompt: ¿Dónde está el periódico? No ___ encuentro.
items.promptEnglish: Where's the newspaper? I can't find it.
items.explanation: el periódico → lo. In a negative sentence the pronoun sits between 'no' and the verb.

items.prompt: Esas flores son bonitas. ___ compro para mi madre.
items.promptEnglish: Those flowers are pretty. I'm buying them for my mother.
items.explanation: las flores → las.

items.prompt: María es mi amiga. ___ veo todos los días.
items.promptEnglish: María is my friend. I see her every day.
items.explanation: A named person as direct object: María → la.

items.prompt: ¿Me escuchas? — Sí, ___ escucho. (a ti)
items.promptEnglish: Are you listening to me? — Yes, I'm listening to you.
items.explanation: First and second person forms don't change for gender: a ti → te.

items.prompt: Mis padres ___ visitan cada domingo. (a nosotros)
items.promptEnglish: My parents visit us every Sunday.
items.explanation: a nosotros → nos.

items.prompt: Necesito los documentos. ¿___ tienes tú?
items.promptEnglish: I need the documents. Do you have them?
items.explanation: los documentos → los.

items.prompt: Estas manzanas están buenas. ¿___ compraste en el mercado?
items.promptEnglish: These apples are good. Did you buy them at the market?
items.explanation: las manzanas → las.

items.prompt: ¿Sabes qué hora es? — No, no ___ sé.
items.promptEnglish: Do you know what time it is? — No, I don't know.
items.explanation: Neuter 'lo' replaces a whole idea or clause, not a noun — hence 'No lo sé', never 'No sé' alone in reply.

items.prompt: 'I'm going to buy the bread.' → ___
items.promptEnglish: I'm going to buy it.
items.explanation: In front of the conjugated verb the pronoun goes before the WHOLE verb phrase, never inside it.

items.prompt: Attach the pronoun instead: "Voy a comprar el pan" → "Voy a ___."
items.promptEnglish: I'm going to buy it.
items.explanation: With an infinitive the pronoun may attach to the end: comprar + lo = comprarlo.

items.prompt: Attach the pronoun to the gerund: "Estoy leyendo el libro" → "Estoy ___."
items.promptEnglish: I'm reading it.
items.explanation: leyendo + lo = leyéndolo. The written accent keeps the original stress.

items.prompt: 'Buy the bread!' → ___
items.promptEnglish: Buy it!
items.explanation: Affirmative commands take the pronoun attached: compra + lo = cómpralo.

items.prompt: 'Don't buy the bread!' → ___
items.promptEnglish: Don't buy it!
items.explanation: Negative commands never attach the pronoun — it goes in front: No lo compres.

items.prompt: "Te voy a ver" y "Voy a verte" — ¿cuál es correcta?
items.promptEnglish: Which is correct: 'Te voy a ver' or 'Voy a verte'?
items.explanation: With an infinitive both positions are equally correct and mean the same thing.

items.prompt: En "Le doy el libro a Juan", ¿cuál es el objeto directo?
items.promptEnglish: In 'Le doy el libro a Juan', which part is the direct object?
items.explanation: The direct object is what is given (el libro). 'A Juan' is the indirect object — the recipient.

items.prompt: Replace the direct object: "Veo a María todos los días" → "___ veo todos los días."
items.promptEnglish: I see her every day.
items.explanation: a María → la.

items.prompt: Replace the direct object: "Escribo las cartas por la noche" → "___ escribo por la noche."
items.promptEnglish: I write them at night.
items.explanation: las cartas → las.

items.prompt: Escribe una pregunta y su respuesta usando un pronombre de objeto directo, como "¿Compraste el pan? — Sí, lo compré".
items.promptEnglish: Write a question and answer using a direct object pronoun, e.g. 'Did you buy the bread? — Yes, I bought it.'
items.guidance: Must contain a question naming a direct object and an answer that replaces it with a direct object pronoun (me/te/lo/la/nos/los/las), correctly agreeing in gender and number and correctly placed. Mark incorrect if the noun is simply repeated instead of replaced, if the pronoun disagrees with the noun (e.g. 'la' for 'el libro'), or if an indirect object pronoun (le/les) is used for a direct object.
items.sampleAnswer: ¿Viste la serie nueva? — Sí, la vi el fin de semana.
items.explanation: The pronoun replaces the direct object and agrees with it in gender and number.
